traits.leaf_area_per_basal_area.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 80 hawthorns: 0.229 m² of leaf a cm². Median leaf area over trunk area at breast height of its open-grown street and park trees 20 cm or more through, the trees the broadleaf median (0.167) was taken over.

traits.crown_spread.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 72 hawthorns 25 years or older: 0.86. Median crown width over height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees.

traits.crown_base_share.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 72 hawthorns 25 years or older: 0.24 (quartiles 0.18 and 0.28). Median height of the crown's base over the tree's height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees, which are often pruned up for clearance.

traits.ovary_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Crataegus by J. B. Phipps (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): perianth and androecium epigynous; carpels partially adnate to the hypanthium, which persists on the pome.

traits.petal_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Crataegus by J. B. Phipps (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals 5, white, more or less circular (elliptic in a few series), the base barely clawed, margins more or less entire.

traits.petal_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Crataegus by J. B. Phipps (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals more or less circular, so their tips are rounded.

traits.thorn_origin.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Crataegus by J. B. Phipps (eFloras, read 2026-10-19, as quoted in the Rosaceae thread's hawthorn note): thorns are modified shoots; indeterminate ones start as lateral or terminal growths and may grow into thorn-tipped shoot systems.

traits.thorn_frequency.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Crataegus by J. B. Phipps (eFloras, read 2026-10-19, as quoted in the Rosaceae thread's hawthorn note): thorns on twigs, few to numerous (var. monogyna); numerous taken as the hawthorns' usual.

traits.thorn_persistence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Crataegus by J. B. Phipps (eFloras, read 2026-10-19, as quoted in the Rosaceae thread's hawthorn note): thorns develop with the new growth and persist a few years.

traits.thorn_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), genus Crataegus by J. B. Phipps (eFloras, read 2026-10-19, as quoted in the Rosaceae thread's hawthorn note): thorns terminal on short shoots (indeterminate) and lateral (determinate).
